transcript.text: When a hob says 'not working properly', it is often something simple like the child lock being engaged. Most hobs have a key or padlock symbol that locks the controls to prevent accidental changes; holding this for a few seconds usually unlocks it. If your hob is induction, it will only work with specific magnetic pans. If you are using a pan that isn't suitable, the zone may not heat up at all or might show an error. Could you tell me if your hob is induction (glass with digital controls) or ceramic/hotplate? Also, do you see a key symbol or padlock icon on the display, and has it been lit up?
It's a ceramic one, Zanussi. No key or padlock showing on the display. Just the rear right ring isn't heating up, the other three are fine.

Since it’s a ceramic hob and only that one zone has failed while the others work perfectly, the most likely cause is that the radiant heating element under the rear right ring has burned out. It could also be the control switch (simmerstat) or wiring for that specific zone, but the element itself is the common failure point. To confirm this safely: please switch off the hob at the wall isolator and wait for it to cool completely. Look closely at the glass under the rear right ring—do you see a visible crack in the ceramic disc underneath, or does the metal coil look broken or discoloured compared to the other rings? If there is no visible damage, we may need an engineer to check the internal wiring and switches.
It's a ceramic hob so the element is under the glass, I can't see it without taking the hob apart and I'm not doing that. The ring doesn't glow red at all though, even with the number showing.

Since that specific ring isn't glowing red at all while the others work fine, it is probably the radiant heating element underneath the glass for that zone has burned out. It could also be the control switch or wiring for that circuit, but the element itself is the most common failure point. Because this part is located under the ceramic surface and requires disconnecting the mains to access safely, you will need a qualified engineer to replace it. Please stop using that specific zone until it has been repaired.
